For the revised literature review. **Checked** says how far each row was verified: *full text* means the paper was read, *partial text* means part of the full text was read, and *abstract* means only the abstract or search snippets were read, so confirm before citing. **Bib key** gives the existing key in `refs/` (— means not in the bib yet).

| Brand, Israeli & Ngwe, "Using LLMs for Market Research" | HBS WP 23-062 (2023); MSI WP 25-136 (Oct 2025); SSRN rev. Apr 2026; no journal acceptance found | Marketing: conjoint (toothpaste, laptops, tablets) | Yes: OpenAI fine-tuning of GPT-3.5 Turbo | Respondent-level conjoint choices from one prior study, as text chat turns (e.g., 300 people × 12 questions = 3,600 examples); one variant adds demographics | No for the target study, but needs a prior study in the same category | Within category: 1A→1B (toothpaste, new flavors), 2A→2B (laptops, new projector feature). Across category: laptops→tablets (2C) | WTP from multinomial logit fit to simulated choices, compared with human WTP | Yes: logit-implied WTP (price-scaled coefficients) | Within category: fine-tuning fixes WTP for new features (projector, new flavors).
